Thanks Hannah — appreciate the agenda. I've attached a short list of questions our infra team wants covered. Quick highlights so you can route to the right engineering folks: 

- How does Redwood handle KV-cache consistency across replicas? (we care about safety for multi-region read-after-write)
- Data residency & encryption: can we pin logs/trace/exported artifacts to our EU region only for certain tenants?
- IAM: SSO + scoped API keys with expiration — is there an audit trail per token?

Sam — thanks for sending these over, good set of items. Below are concise, actionable answers we can present in the session; I've noted owners for follow-ups and whether we'd add a slide.

1) KV-cache consistency across replicas — short answer: strong read-after-write per-shard with eventual cross-region sync.
   - Details: we keep write affinity to a primary shard; local reads hit the primary or an L1 cache depending on routing policy. Cross-region replication is async but we commit a log with causal metadata so clients can opt into read-your-writes semantics per-tenant.
   - Owner: Dev (engineering) will add a diagram. Slide: yes (cache-consistency.png).

2) Data residency & encryption (pinning logs/traces) — short answer: supports region-scoped retention and encryption keys (KMS integration).
   - Details: control plane lets you tag tenants and route their telemetry to a region-local storage bucket. We offer HSM/KMS integrations for key isolation; exports can be restricted via RBAC. Note: private deployments (VPC/on-prem) provide stronger guarantees.
   - Owner: Jonas (security) for KMS details. Slide: yes (data-residency.pdf).

3) IAM, SSO & token audit trail — short answer: SSO + scoped API keys supported; full token audit logs available to enterprise customers.
   - Details: tokens have TTL and scopes, and we maintain an append-only audit log with token usage by route/model. Logs are available via the console and can be forwarded to the customer's SIEM.
   - Owner: Marissa (PM) to confirm retention windows; follow-up required. Slide: short bullet + link to audit-export doc.

4) Failover behavior & latency delta — short answer: automatic fallback to compatible model variants or region fallback; expected additional P50 latency in the 20-70ms range depending on model size and network hop.
   - Details: policy-based routing triggers fallback paths (regional replica, cheaper quantized variant) with graceful degradation. We'll show a decision tree during the call.
   - Owner: Dev to prepare decision tree. Slide: yes (fallback-decision-tree.png).

5) Quantization profiles — short answer: we recommend mixed-precision 8-bit for production reads; we provide per-model accuracy regressions from our Optimize toolkit to help pick the profile.
   - Details: initial recommendation is 8-bit PTQ for throughput-first workloads, and 4-bit (q4) for cost-sensitive probes with eval gating. We'll show a short table of accuracy delta vs latency.
   - Owner: Jonas + Research to provide numbers; Marissa to include recommended defaults. Slide: yes (quant-profiles.xlsx).

I've attached the draft slides and will incorporate Dev's diagrams. If anything needs more depth pre-call, flag it and I'll expand.

Attachments: rdw-slides-draft.pptx
